summary: A second independent review of the start screen and guides (regressions, hands-on flows, wording; then skeptics) confirmed 16 more problems, and all are fixed. The guides now always point you at a step you can do right away, and their instructions name buttons that are really on the page.
points: "Do step N", Next and Skip pick a step you can do now, never one that waits on a step you skipped while another is free.
Buy a home asks for your pay first, so Home affordability can show your price range the moment you arrive.
Five instructions named buttons that were folded away or did not exist (Federal estimate, Consolidation, Student loans, State, filing status); they now say what is really on screen.
Changing a choice list or a tick box no longer sets off the "you have unsaved typing" warning (the bank-file page's account picker did).
A finished guide shows its link once instead of four times.
Home affordability's "Make it a goal" no longer overwrites a goal like "Home repairs": the page and the guide share one test for the house goal.
numbers: 16 findings confirmed by the skeptics, all fixed

shots.caption: Buy a home now starts with your pay; the goal step says it needs step 2, and "Do step 2" opens your price range.
A finished guide: one filled button, one outlined, and a link to see all the steps.
